To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Ca2+ is essential for opioid receptor recognition, the Ca(2+) complexes of opioid peptides with mu-affinity resemble Ca(2+) complex of morphine and Ca(2+) is essential for the binding of morphine to the mu-opioid receptors.

(i) Ca(2+) binds to Met-enkephaline and morphine in a very similar manner; (ii) the Ca(2+) bound form of the peptide is the most active form; and (iii) the Ca(3+)-bound form of morphine and opioid peptides with high mu-opioid activity is similar to the Ca(2)-bound form of the peptide, whereas the Ca(2+)/Ca(2+) form of opioid peptides with low mu
Ca2+ binding to opioid peptides is accompanied by a conformational change of the ligand, which is the key factor in ligand-receptors interactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of Ca(2+) in opioid receptor recognition, the structure of opioid receptor binding sites, and the structure-activity relationships of opioid peptides and drugs.
understanding how the structure of a ligand determines its affinity to the receptor.
the structure of opioid peptides, their interactions with opioid receptors and with the opioid receptor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ca(2+) complex of the mu-receptor agonist morphine is the only opioid peptide that can be found in the Ca(2+)/mu-receptor complex.
Ca(2+) is a structural determinant of mu-receptor binding, and that the conformational flexibility of opioid peptides is restricted in the presence of the divalent ion.
the opioid receptor is a mu receptor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ca2+ is involved in the recognition of the ligand by the mu-opioid receptor, and that this recognition is based on the conformational similarity of the Ca2+-bound ligand to Ca2+-bound morphine.
the Ca2+ binding is an essential component of the opioid receptor recognition.
the mu-receptor recognizes the Ca2+-bound form of opioid ligands, and the mu-receptor-ligand recognition involves the Ca2+ complex of the mu-receptor itself.
The main takeaway from our work is that
opioid ligands with high mu-affinities are likely to bind to opioid receptors in the Ca(2+) bound form.
the Ca2+-binding ability of a peptide is an important determinant of its affinity for the mu-opioid receptor.
the conformation of Ca(2+), bound to a peptide, may be used as a probe to determine the conformation of the peptide in solution.
